axes.model_access: Digital-human video generation line: Avatar (digital-human persona) + Voice (dubbing/cloning) + Translation (video translation/lip-sync) — three product lines (as seen in site navigation); the underlying models — no official statement verified item by item.
axes.runtime: Web (heygen.com) + API (an API entry on the official site, enterprise-facing); generation on the vendor's cloud.
axes.local_files: Works stored account-side in the cloud, generation history visible on the web works page; downloads go local. No officially stated local data surface.
axes.background: Generation is instant/queued (varies by tier, not verified item by item); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" task surface (no claim verified).
axes.tools: A digital-human persona library + real-person cloning (with a consent surface), voice cloning, **video translation + lip-sync** (multilingual localization is the flagship scenario), an interactive digital-human line (seen on the official site); template/script-driven workflows.
axes.context: Organized by projects/brand spaces (the enterprise surface); cross-session memory — no official statement verified. Digital-human assets are its "consistency" mechanism.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription + enterprise system (D9: prices not collected); **the consent and verification mechanism for cloning real personas/voices is the key compliance surface** (the official side has a consent-flow narrative, details not verified line by line).
axes.fit: Fits: enterprise training/marketing video localization (translation + lip-sync), replacing on-camera talent (consented cloning), batch talking-head videos. Does not fit: creative narrative generation, entertainment with obvious AI-look, cloning others without consent (a terms red line).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

related: The two enterprise digital-human heavyweights: Synthesia is more corporate training-oriented, HeyGen more flexible on cloning and translation.
Both digital-human talking heads: D-ID is light on photo-driven, HeyGen's product line is wider.
Another species of video generation: Runway builds visuals, HeyGen builds "people talking".
API downstream: HeyGen's API often reaches content pipelines through Zapier-style platforms — batch localization only scales that way.
